Split tracks into trips for central place foragers

Source: R/tt_split_trips.R
tt_split_trips.Rd

This function splits tracks into trips for central place foragers, based on when the animal moves away from, and returns to, the colony/nest (the centre). A trip is an excursion beyond buffer_trip, with no minimum duration (a single location beyond it is a trip); gaps in the data do not split trips.

Trips are classified as complete or incomplete. If the track starts or ends beyond buffer_trip, i.e. during a trip, that trip is incomplete (e.g. the logger only started recording after the animal had left, or its battery failed before the animal returned). So only the first and last trips of a track can be incomplete, and a track that starts and ends at the centre only has complete trips.

buffer_complete can make this check more tolerant. If it is larger than buffer_trip, it is used instead, so a trip is only incomplete if the track starts or ends beyond buffer_complete. For example, with buffer_trip = 10 km and buffer_complete = 50 km, a track that starts 30 km from the centre has a complete first trip. If buffer_complete is the same as, or smaller than, buffer_trip, it has no effect.

Usage

tt_split_trips(
  x,
  centre_col = NULL,
  buffer_trip = as_units(1000, "m"),
  buffer_complete = as_units(1000, "m"),
  complete = TRUE,
  boundary_events = c("none", "return", "departure", "both"),
  buffer_outbound = NULL,
  buffer_inbound = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A move2 object

centre_col

character string, the name of the column in the metadata table that contains the centre of the colony/nest for each track. This column must be of class sfc_POINT and should have a valid coordinate reference system (CRS) specified. The function sf_point_col() can be used to create this column.

buffer_trip

the distance from the centre that delimits trips: a trip starts when the animal moves further than this distance from the centre, and ends when it comes back within it. Specified as a unit object, e.g as_units(10000, "m") or as_units(10, "km").

buffer_complete

a distance from the centre, usually the same as or larger than buffer_trip, within which a track can start or end during a trip and that trip still be classified as complete (see Description). It has no effect if it is the same as, or smaller than, buffer_trip. Specified as a unit object, e.g as_units(10000, "m") or as_units(10, "km").

complete

boolean, if TRUE, only complete trips are kept. If FALSE, all trips are kept, and events at the colony (i.e. in-between trips) are collected into a dummy trip labelled "trip_na".

boundary_events

which locations at the centre, i.e. within buffer_trip, are also included in the trips, so that the trips connect to the centre:

  • "none" (the default): none, trips only include the events outside buffer_trip.

  • "return": each trip that ends back at the centre also includes the location that ends it, i.e. its first location back within buffer_trip, as the trips of tripSplit() in the track2KBA package do.

  • "departure": each trip that does not start the track also includes its departure location, i.e. the last location within buffer_trip before it.

  • "both": both of the above. If a single location at the centre separates two trips, it is the return of the earlier trip, and the later trip has no departure location.

Trips that start or end the track have no departure or return location.

buffer_outbound, buffer_inbound

Deprecated, use buffer_trip and buffer_complete instead (see tidytracks-deprecated). The old names still work for backwards compatibility, but they issue a warning and will be removed in a future release.

Value

The move2 object, modified: each track is split into its foraging trips, and each trip is treated as a separate track:

  • The events have a new column, trip_id, which becomes the track id column. The original track id column is kept, so trips can still be grouped by track.

  • The metadata has one row per trip, with the columns of its original track (repeated for each of its trips), and new columns trip_id (linking to events table trip_id), and trip_type:

    • "complete": the whole trip was recorded.

    • "incomplete": the track starts or ends during the trip (beyond buffer_complete, if that is larger than buffer_trip), so part of the trip is missing.

    • "at_centre": not a trip, but all the events of the track at the centre (before, between and after its trips), in a single row per track.

Trips are labelled <track id>_trip_1, <track id>_trip_2, ... in time order, and <track id>_trip_na for the events at the centre. With complete = TRUE (the default), only complete trips are kept, so tracks without a complete trip are dropped, and the numbering can have gaps (e.g. if the first trip of a track is incomplete, its first trip kept is <track id>_trip_2).

Details

Events without a location (empty geometries) are assigned to the trip of the preceding event with a location (or of the following one, at the start of a track), so they only join a trip when they fall between two of its events. In particular, events without a location after a return location added by boundary_events stay at the centre.

Examples

# First, add a sf point column to metadata giving nest location
show_meta(example_tt) <- show_meta(example_tt) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(nest_location = sf_point_col(nest_lon, nest_lat, crs = 4326))
# Now split the tracks into trips
example_tt_split <- tt_split_trips(
  x = example_tt,
  centre_col = "nest_location",
  buffer_trip = as_units(1, "km"),
  buffer_complete = as_units(1, "km"),
  complete = FALSE
)
# Now the unit of tracking is `trip_id` column
move2::mt_track_id_column(example_tt_split)
#> [1] "trip_id"
# Three incomplete trips were identified
show_meta(example_tt_split) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(track_id, trip_id, trip_type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   track_id trip_id   trip_type 
#>   <fct>    <chr>     <chr>     
#> 1 a        a_trip_1  incomplete
#> 2 b        b_trip_1  incomplete
#> 3 b        b_trip_na at_centre 
#> 4 c        c_trip_1  incomplete
#> 5 c        c_trip_na at_centre
